header.contentArea: Consent for risk-reducing gynaecological surgery in a BRCA carrier
guidelineVersions: GMC: Decision making and consent (In effect 9 November 2020; updated 13 December 2024 and 3 August 2026)
NICE CG164: Familial breast cancer (Published June 2013; last updated November 2023)

related.why: The earlier conversation where this option was first discussed
The wider family context around her BRCA2 diagnosis

brief.role: Trainee supporting the gynaecology consent process
brief.scenario: Ms Linford, 44, a confirmed BRCA2 carrier who has completed her family, has decided to proceed with risk-reducing bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy.
brief.task: Consent her for this surgery. You have 7 minutes.

beforeYouWalkIn.frame: Confirm she has completed family planning and understands the procedure, then cover surgical menopause and HRT, then risks and voluntariness.
beforeYouWalkIn.trap: Explaining the surgical risks without discussing surgical menopause, which is often the aspect that most affects her day-to-day life afterwards.
beforeYouWalkIn.firstMove: "Before we go through consent, can I check where things stand with family planning, since this surgery will end that permanently?"

grid.label: Confirming family planning is complete
grid.fail: Does not check whether she has completed family planning before proceeding.
grid.pass: Explicitly confirms she has finished having children and understands this surgery is not reversible in that respect.
grid.high: Checks this sensitively, recognising it may carry emotional weight even if her family planning is genuinely complete.

grid.label: Explaining the procedure
grid.fail: Cannot describe what the operation involves.
grid.pass: Explains that both ovaries and fallopian tubes will be removed, usually laparoscopically.
grid.high: Mentions that tissue removed will be examined for any early, currently undetected cancer, as this is standard practice in risk-reducing surgery.

grid.label: Surgical menopause and HRT
grid.fail: Does not mention that this surgery causes immediate surgical menopause.
grid.pass: Explains that removing both ovaries causes immediate menopause, with symptoms such as hot flushes, and that hormone replacement therapy can be considered to manage this.
grid.high: Explains HRT is generally appropriate up to the natural age of menopause for BRCA carriers without hormone-sensitive cancer, and that her own breast cancer history will need individual thought.

grid.label: Surgical risks
grid.fail: Lists only generic laparoscopic risks with nothing specific to this operation.
grid.pass: Covers risks including bleeding, infection, damage to surrounding organs, and the certainty of surgical menopause.
grid.high: Explains rare but recognised risks (e.g. conversion to open surgery, bowel or bladder injury) proportionate to what a reasonable patient would want to know.

grid.label: Voluntariness
grid.fail: Assumes her earlier interest in this option means consent is a formality today.
grid.pass: Checks she remains certain and is deciding voluntarily, without pressure.
grid.high: Explicitly offers to pause or delay if she has any hesitation, even at this late stage.

grid.label: Documentation and closing
grid.fail: Completes consent with no mention of documentation or what happens next.
grid.pass: Confirms her decision, documents consent, and explains next practical steps.
grid.high: Checks she has a plan in place for managing menopausal symptoms and support at home after surgery.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: So, ovaries and tubes out, standard risks, sign here.

fail.speaker: patient
fail.text: Will I go through menopause straight away?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Before we go through consent, can I check - are you certain your family is complete? This surgery will end that permanently.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: We'll remove both ovaries and fallopian tubes, usually with keyhole surgery.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Removing your ovaries brings on immediate menopause, so you may notice symptoms like hot flushes straight away - hormone replacement therapy is an option to manage this, which we can discuss.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Risks include bleeding, infection, and a small risk of injury to nearby organs, alongside the certain effect of surgical menopause.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Are you still happy to go ahead, and is this entirely your own decision?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I'll document your consent, and let's talk about your plan for managing symptoms afterwards.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Before consent, I want to check sensitively - are you certain your family is complete? This will end that permanently, and I want to make sure that's something you've fully considered.

high.speaker: patient
high.text: Yes, completely certain, we've talked about it a lot.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: We'll remove both ovaries and tubes laparoscopically, and the tissue will be examined afterwards, as standard, in case there's any very early change not visible beforehand.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: This will bring on immediate surgical menopause, with symptoms like hot flushes. Given your history of breast cancer, we'll need to think carefully with you about whether hormone replacement is appropriate, which is a slightly different conversation than for someone without that history.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Beyond the certainty of surgical menopause, risks include bleeding, infection, and rarely, injury to the bowel or bladder or needing to convert to open surgery.

high.speaker: patient
high.text: I do still want to go ahead.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: That's good to hear, but I want you to know we can still pause or delay this even now if anything changes for you.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I'll document your consent. Do you have a plan for support at home, and have you thought about how you'll manage symptoms in the early weeks?

failures.move: Failing to explain that surgical menopause is immediate and certain, not a possible future risk.
failures.consequence: Leaves her unprepared for symptoms that begin right after surgery, undermining informed consent for one of the most significant effects of the operation.

failures.move: Not confirming family planning is complete before proceeding.
failures.consequence: Risks proceeding with an irreversible decision without confirming she has fully considered its permanence.

failures.move: Treating consent as a formality because she expressed interest at an earlier appointment.
failures.consequence: Assumes consent carries over from an earlier conversation rather than being reconfirmed at the time of the decision.

failures.move: Cannot describe what the operation actually involves, e.g. dismissing it as "ovaries and tubes out".
failures.consequence: Leaves her unable to picture the operation or ask informed questions before consenting.

failures.move: Ending the consultation with no mention of documentation or next steps.
failures.consequence: No record of the discussion exists, and she is left without practical next steps before surgery.

recovery.when: You didn't mention surgical menopause is immediate
recovery.line: I should be clear - this menopause starts right away after surgery, not gradually.

recovery.when: You assumed her earlier interest meant consent was settled
recovery.line: Let me actually check with you now - are you still certain you want to go ahead?

knowledge.fact: Risk-reducing bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy causes immediate surgical menopause, distinct from the gradual onset of natural menopause.

Hormone replacement therapy is generally considered appropriate for BRCA carriers up to the natural age of menopause, though individual factors, including personal cancer history, are taken into account.
Removed ovarian and tubal tissue from risk-reducing surgery is routinely examined histologically for any early, occult malignancy.

recall.think: Confirm family planning is complete; menopause is immediate, not gradual; reconfirm consent now.
recall.say: "We can still pause this if anything changes for you."
do: Confirm family planning is genuinely complete first
Explain immediate surgical menopause; discuss HRT given her cancer history
Reconfirm voluntary consent rather than assuming it

numbers.meaning: earliest recommended age for risk-reducing surgery in BRCA2 carriers, once family planning is complete

recall.trap: Treating consent as already settled, or not flagging that menopause will be immediate, not gradual.
recall.finish: Reconfirmed, documented consent with a surgical-menopause management plan.

partner.opening: Please take consent from this patient for risk-reducing bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy. You have 7 minutes.
partner.actorBrief: You are Rachel Linford, 44, a confirmed BRCA2 carrier who has decided to proceed with this surgery, having completed your family. You are prepared for the operation but haven't fully thought through the immediacy of surgical menopause.

reveals.trigger: Candidate confirms family planning is complete
reveals.finding: You confirm this with certainty, having discussed it with your partner.

reveals.trigger: Candidate explains surgical menopause is immediate
reveals.finding: You're surprised it starts right away rather than gradually, and ask more questions.

reveals.trigger: Candidate reconfirms your voluntary decision rather than assuming it
reveals.finding: You appreciate being asked again rather than assumed.

push.question: Will I go into menopause straight away?
push.expect: Confirm menopause begins immediately after surgery, not gradually, and discuss HRT as an option.

push.question: Can I take hormone replacement, given my breast cancer history?
push.expect: Acknowledge this needs individual consideration given her cancer history, rather than a blanket yes or no.

curveballs.prompt: What if I change my mind on the operating table?
curveballs.safeAnswer: Confirm that consent can be withdrawn at any point up to the point of surgery.

curveballs.prompt: Will this surgery find anything unexpected?
curveballs.safeAnswer: Explain that tissue removed will be examined and, though uncommon, an early undetected cancer could occasionally be found, which is part of why the surgery is done as a preventive measure.
